techniques.why: additive harmonic stack -- the general-purpose way to build any harmonic instrument colour: a seven-harmonic gbuzz stack doubled by a twin three cents above, so the pair beats slowly; knh sets how many partials, kmul how fast they fall away
techniques.code:
kad0    poscil 0.0004, 0.053         ; slow drift, upper stack
aa10    gbuzz 0.52, (kfreq * koct1), 7, 1, 0.68, giCos          ; harmonic stack
aa20    gbuzz 0.34, (kfreq * koct1) * (1.0018 + kad0), 7, 1, 0.64, giCos ; twin, +3 cents
asig    = aa10 + aa20

techniques.why: bell / church bell / chime / carillon / tubular bell: true inharmonic bell partials (h 2.76/5.4/8.93) written as 2-operator FM at a 1.41 ratio, so the partials sit off the harmonic grid instead of being projected onto it

index.note: the peak FM index: how many sidebands the tone carries -- how bright and rich it is. As it rises the spectrum brightens steeply while the loudness stays constant (a balance stage holds the level), so only the colour moves, never the volume.

mellow.gloss: few sidebands, close to a pure sine -- soft and round

bright.gloss: a full, singing brightness with rich sidebands

harsh.gloss: hard and edgy, the sidebands crowding the top

screaming.gloss: the brightest, most aggressive FM -- sidebands to the ceiling

ring.note: how long the bright attack rings before the tone darkens. Every FM note begins bright and loses its highs as it is held -- never its loudness. Low collapses to a dark body almost at once; high stays bright deep into the note.

quick.gloss: the brightness collapses almost at once, leaving a dark body

medium.gloss: the bright attack settles into a darker sustain

long.gloss: stays bright well into the note before it darkens

detune.note: a second voice offset a fixed few Hz above the first, so the two drift against each other and the tone undulates. At 0 it stands perfectly still (the static escape); higher is a wider, more present movement. The offset is fixed in HERTZ, so it is the same at every pitch -- not a cent detune that scales with the note, and not pitch vibrato, which belongs to the synth.

pure.gloss: a single still tone, the two voices locked together

gentle.gloss: a slow gentle drift between the two voices

techniques.why: electric piano / rhodes / wurlitzer / dx piano: a struck tine or reed body with a metallic attack that fades back into it; ting = how much metal is in the strike, ring = how long it rings, reed = full body to hollow reed, strike = how hard the hammer hits

ting.note: the metallic 'ting' of the attack. this is the single feature that separates an electric piano from a plain fm tone; at 0 the instrument is only its wooden body. the ting fades back into the body as the note is held -- it loses its brightness, never its loudness.

none.gloss: no metal at all, just the woody body

soft.gloss: a faint chime on the attack

clangy.gloss: a hard bright metallic clang on every note

ring.note: how long the metallic part keeps ringing before it settles into the body. short is a quick struck-tine click, long is a sustained metallic buzz that stays through the note. both ends are taken from real electric pianos: the short end is a rhodes-like tine, the long end a wurlitzer-like reed.

short.gloss: a quick click, gone almost at once

long.gloss: a metallic buzz that stays through the note

hollowness.note: the body's character, from full to hollow. low keeps every harmonic and sounds broad and piano-like; high keeps only the odd harmonics, which is what makes a reed sound hollow and nasal. 'tine' is where a classic electric piano sits.

full.gloss: broad and full, every harmonic present

tine.gloss: the classic tine electric piano body

reed.gloss: hollow and nasal, a reed rather than a tine

strike.note: how hard the hammer hits: how bright the body starts before it softens. this shapes the tone, not the volume -- a hard strike is brighter, not louder.

soft.gloss: mellow and round from the first moment

hard.gloss: struck hard, bright and biting before it settles

techniques.why: three-operator phase modulation: TWO modulators driving one carrier's phase in linear combination, so the spectrum carries two sideband families and the drive travels back and forth BETWEEN them. That travel is what two operators cannot do -- with one modulator a control can only make its single family stronger or weaker, never trade it for a different one. Method: Chowning, JAES 21(7), 1973; the topology and the word-to-parameter directions from Hayes & Saitis 2020, thirty sound designers on exactly this layout. Csound 6.18 has no generic N-operator opcode, so the two modulators are summed into a `phasor` and read through `tablei`. BJ's reading of the setting this was found at, 2026-07-30: bassoon-like, with a kind of pulse-width modulation -- the `fm` entry beside it reads Rhodes-like. It is NOT a bassoon and does not claim to be one; that reading is what two families trading sounds like at ratio 1.0. DECLARED, and the first thing to know before routing it as a melodic voice: the body transposes exactly with `kfreq`, but WHICH OCTAVE it sounds in is set by `ratio 3`. With `ratio 2` at 1.0 a half-integer `ratio 3` puts the whole spectrum on a grid of `kfreq`/2, so the note sounds an OCTAVE BELOW the key -- measured f0 exactly `kfreq`/2 at 1.5, 2.5, 3.5, 4.5, 5.5 and 6.5, and exactly `kfreq` at 2, 3, 4, 6, 7 and 8, at every register from 55 to 1760 Hz. That subharmonic grid is a setting the axis offers, not the one it ships on: the default is 6.0 and plays the key (+0 ct measured). DECLARED: it STANDS -- the host owns the note-off, so unlike `fm`/`fm_bell`/`metallic_fm` there is no index decay ringing it down (sustain 0.996 to 0.999 across six registers). The spectrum is HARMONIC at every setting: 1.3 to 2.1 % of the energy off the series, measured against the grid the body actually has. An earlier reading of this entry reported 59 to 64 % "off-series" and called the axis an alternation between harmonic and inharmonic -- that was the partials counted against the KEY on a body sounding an octave below it, i.e. the signature of the subharmonic above and not of inharmonicity. What alternates along `ratio 3` is the sounding octave, not the harmonicity. Hayes & Saitis report that on this topology `bright` and `rough` load on the same parameter moves, so a setting cannot be made brighter without also being heard as rougher; that is their finding on their data. Nothing in this repository measures either word, so it is not restated here as a measurement -- reach for this entry for brightness and for two-family movement, and treat roughness as untested. THE MOVEMENT IS IN THE SUSTAIN, and that has to be said because the platform's own movement meter reads the whole note and a spectral attack alone can satisfy it: with the trade frozen this body reads 105 cents over the note and 0 through the sustain, so its onset alone would clear the 60-cent threshold. Running, it reads 748 cents through the sustain at the default (307 to 1405 across the axes). The band is bounded by Carson's rule SUMMED over both operators -- carrier + (I+1)*fm each, both spending the same room -- and the whole drive is scaled by one factor when it does not fit, so the balance between the families and the FRACTION that travels survive the bound. Bounding each operator as if it were alone let the travelling drive arrive on top of an already-full index: at ratio 8/8, both indices 0.6 and `trade` 0.75 on a 440 Hz note at sr 44100 that put a sideband at 49 kHz and 42.7 % of the energy off the grid, against 1.4 % now. The cost of the bound is at the top of the keyboard: above about 880 Hz the drive is scaled down and the body thins toward a sine (centroid 6050 Hz at 880, 5489 at 1760). Two operators on exactly the SAME ratio are one oscillator with a constant total drive and have nothing to trade: unguarded, the diagonal moves 0 to 9 cents through the sustain. A separation of 0.01 already moves 1130, so the guard fires only within 0.02 and pushes toward the middle of the range, which reaches 0.7 % of the ratio plane and cannot leave the declared range. The trade oscillator is FREE-RUNNING and the note-on does not reset it, which is the platform's own rule for a loop -- so two notes played minutes apart start at different points in the breath, and the first window's colour differs by up to 375 Hz depending on how long the plugin has been open. Loudness inside a note: 0.01 to 0.19 dB at 220 Hz across all six axes, 0.03 to 0.20 dB at 55 Hz. GATED 2026-07-30 (`tools/lco_axis_probe.py --gate`, 729 corners x 6 registers, at the gate's sr 44100): every corner renders, moves and holds one loudness -- loudness spread 0.03 dB across the corners, 0.0 dB across the registers, 0.03 dB crossed, worst peak 0.66 against the host's 2.52. It reports 339 of 3645 corner-renders away from 220 Hz that do not move, 338 of them at 1760 Hz: at sr 44100 the band ends eleven harmonics above an 1760 Hz note, and two sideband families at high ratios do not fit in it at all, so the band bound scales the drive to nothing. That is the gate's rate, not the instrument's -- re-rendered at the plugin's default 176400 the same corners move 1066 to 1151 cents. Nearest existing entry, and what it was heard against: `fm`.
techniques.code:
kc      = kfreq * koct1
kr2     = 1.00   ; ratio 2[1.0..8.0]: operator 2's tuning ratio -- a whole number is harmonic, between them not
kr3     = 6.00   ; ratio 3[1.0..8.0]: operator 3's ratio, the second family
ki2     = 0.26   ; index 2[0.0..0.6]: how deep operator 2 drives, in CYCLES of carrier phase
ki3     = 0.20   ; index 3[0.0..0.6]: how deep operator 3 drives
ktrd    = 0.21   ; trade[0.20..0.75]: what FRACTION of the drive travels between the two operators.
                 ;   A fraction and not an amount, so it means the same at any depth: a fixed amount
                 ;   is swamped once both indices are deep. The floor is not zero -- a body always
                 ;   trades a little. The floor is set by the THINNEST body, not by this default:
                 ;   with both indices at zero, 0.10 leaves two ratio settings static and 0.20 does not
kons    = 0.05   ; onset[0.002..0.6]: seconds the sidebands need to arrive -- a SPECTRAL attack
kr3g    = (abs(kr3 - kr2) < 0.02 ? (kr2 > 4.5 ? kr2 - 1.75 : kr2 + 1.75) : kr3)  ; two operators
                                            ;   on exactly the SAME ratio are ONE oscillator with a
                                            ;   constant total drive, so there is nothing to trade:
                                            ;   measured, the diagonal moves 0 to 9 cents through the
                                            ;   sustain. A separation of 0.01 already moves 1130, so
                                            ;   only true coincidence is escaped -- and TOWARDS the
                                            ;   middle, so the push cannot leave the declared range
kdrv    = ki2 + ki3 + 0.20                  ; the drive there is to share, plus a floor so a body
                                            ;   with both indices at zero still has something to trade
ktr     = ktrd * kdrv                       ; the amount that travels, before the band is consulted
kpk2    = max(ki2 + ktr, 0.001)             ; what an operator PEAKS at is its own index PLUS all of
kpk3    = max(ki3 + ktr, 0.001)             ;   the travelling drive -- both arrive on one operator
kroom   limit min(sr * 0.45, 20000) / kc - 1 - kr2 - kr3g, 0, 4000  ; the room the BAND leaves above the two
                                            ;   modulators' first pair. Carson's rule per operator,
                                            ;   summed: (I+1)*fm each, and they spend the SAME room.
                                            ;   Bounding each operator as if it were alone is what put
                                            ;   a 49 kHz sideband on a 440 Hz note at sr 44100
kneed   = 6.2832 * (kpk2 * kr2 + kpk3 * kr3g)   ; radians, so cycles * 2pi
kscl    = min(1, kroom / kneed)              ; one factor for all three, so the balance between the
                                            ;   families and the FRACTION that travels survive it
ki2c    = ki2 * kscl
ki3c    = ki3 * kscl
ktrc    = ktr * kscl
ksw     oscili 0.5, 0.45, giSine            ; free-running, 2.2 s -- more than one cycle in a 3 s note
kt2     = ktrc * (0.5 + ksw)                ; the SAME drive, moving from operator 2 ...
kt3     = ktrc * (0.5 - ksw)                ;   ... to operator 3 and back. Not a level wobble:
karr    = min(knote / kons, 1)              ;   what changes is WHICH family carries the spectrum
am2     poscil (ki2c + kt2) * karr, kc * kr2, giSine
am3     poscil (ki3c + kt3) * karr, kc * kr3g, giSine
aph     phasor kc
apm     = aph + am2 + am3
acar    tablei apm, giSine, 1, 0, 1
aref    poscil 0.45, kc                     ; steady level reference

                                            ;   on a 55 Hz note a 1 Hz follower cannot keep up

index 3.note: how deep operator 3 drives -- the brightness axis, and the one that matches Hayes & Saitis's measured direction. dark.gloss: the far family silent; only the near one speaks, 792 Hz

bright.gloss: the far family carrying the spectrum, 3149 Hz

glaring.gloss: as bright as the band allows, 3865 Hz

ratio 2.note: operator 2's tuning ratio to the carrier -- where the NEAR family sits. Measured at 220 Hz: centroid 1698 -> 1922 -> 2097 -> 3117 Hz at 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 8.0. It does not have to be kept away from `ratio 3`, only off it: a separation of 0.01 already moves 1130 cents through the sustain, while exact coincidence makes the two operators one oscillator with nothing to trade (0 to 9 cents). working.gloss: 1171 cents -- the two families clearly taking turns

restless.gloss: the whole drive changing hands, centroid up to 2878 Hz

heard.bj_wortlaut: fm3 habe ich nicht abgenommen, überhaupt nur ein paar files gehört
heard.hinweis: 2026-07-30: trägt zusätzlich die Oberflächenformen des gestrichenen Eintrags `fm` (fm, frequency modulation, phase modulation, operator …), weil das Verfahren hier weiterlebt und das Wort sonst ins Leere liefe. NICHT übernommen: „2 op fm“ / „2 operator fm“ — das benennt eine Konstruktion, die dieser Eintrag nicht ist.

techniques.why: a chain of three phase-modulation operators with an envelope on each and feedback on the middle one -- the DX7's own construction rather than a prefabricated two-operator block. Operator 3 drives operator 2, operator 2 drives the carrier and also its own phase; each operator's drive falls at its own rate, so the spectrum does not merely get darker, it changes shape while the note is held. A modulator that is itself modulated is what no number of parallel operators can produce, and the feedback path takes the top operator from a sine through a saw to noise.

depth.note: how deep operator 2 drives the carrier, in cycles of phase. At zero nothing reaches the carrier and the body is a bare sine -- the static escape. Rising, the sidebands spread and the tone brightens steeply, while a balance stage holds the level, so only the colour moves.

bare.gloss: no modulation at all: a bare sine, and the only still setting

soft.gloss: a few sidebands, rounded and close to the fundamental

full.gloss: the full body, sidebands well up the spectrum

driven.gloss: driven to the top: the widest spread this chain reaches

feedback.note: how far operator 2 modulates its own phase. This is the DX7's own feedback path and it is the widest single character change in the body: at zero the modulator is a sine, rising it becomes a sawtooth and beyond that it breaks into noise. It also carries most of the movement in a held note.

clean.gloss: the modulator is a pure sine: the tidiest, most orderly spectrum

edged.gloss: a first sawtooth lean on the modulator, sidebands thickening

rough.gloss: clearly rough, the spectrum crowded and restless

broken.gloss: broken into noise: the operator no longer holds a shape

ratio.note: operator 2's tuning against the played note. A whole number puts every sideband on a harmonic of the note and the body reads as a pitched instrument; between whole numbers the sidebands fall off the harmonic series and the body reads as metal or glass. The two off-series anchors are NOT free choices: they are the ratios `fm_bell` (1.41) and `metallic_fm` (2.41) already stand on in this library. A ratio further off the series -- 3.47 was tried -- dissolves into a noise band once `depth` is high, which BJ heard on 2026-07-30 and rejected: „das pinke rauschen bei rough ist nicht musikalisch“. A ratio is NOT a transposition: a modulator at 2 puts nothing at the octave and one at 3 puts nothing at the twelfth. It decides WHICH partials survive -- at 2 the even ones cancel, at 3 the multiples of three do. The anchors are named for the set that is left.

unison.gloss: on the note: the most harmonic, most pitched setting

bell.gloss: the bell ratio -- the same 1.41 `fm_bell` is built on, sidebands off the series but still a countable set

odd only.gloss: the even partials cancel: 1 3 5 7 9 11 13, hollow, the square-wave colour. Nothing sounds an octave up -- at twice the note the modulator does not transpose, it removes the even partials

metal.gloss: the metal ratio -- the same 2.41 `metallic_fm` is built on: gong and bowl territory

high.gloss: far up: a thin bright band above the note

stack.note: how much operator 3 drives operator 2. This is the chain proper: the modulator is itself modulated, so its own spectrum widens before it ever reaches the carrier. At zero the body is a plain two-operator voice with feedback; rising, it takes on the dense second-order sidebands no parallel operator can make.

none.gloss: operator 3 silent: a plain two-operator voice

light.gloss: the modulator just beginning to be modulated

full.gloss: the chain fully in play, dense second-order sidebands

piled.gloss: piled on: the modulator is itself a complex tone

ratio hi.note: operator 3's tuning. It sets where the second-order sidebands land around operator 2's own frequency, so it colours the modulator rather than the carrier -- the difference between a bright harmonic stack and a clangy one is usually here. A ratio is NOT a transposition: a modulator at 2 puts nothing at the octave and one at 3 puts nothing at the twelfth. It decides WHICH partials survive -- at 2 the even ones cancel, at 3 the multiples of three do. The anchors are named for the set that is left.

low.gloss: below the modulator: slow, wide beating inside the drive

unison.gloss: on the modulator: the tightest, most harmonic stack

dark.gloss: the same harmonic set as on the modulator, but measurably darker: centroid 684 Hz against 1095 at `unison`, because the Nyquist guard spends less drive on a modulator standing twice as high

metal.gloss: off the series, on `metallic_fm`'s ratio: the drive itself becomes inharmonic

decay.note: how long each operator's drive holds before it falls back to its floor. Every operator has its own rate, the higher one faster, so this is not one brightness fading: the balance between the two modulators shifts while the note is held. Low is a struck attack that collapses at once; high holds the full spectrum deep into the note.

struck.gloss: the drive collapses almost at once, leaving a dark body

short.gloss: a brief bright head, then the body

held.gloss: the spectrum holds well into the note

standing.gloss: barely falls: the full drive stands

onset.note: seconds the sidebands need to arrive -- a spectral attack, not a level attack. Short is a strike; long is a tone that opens.

strike.gloss: the spectrum is there at once

opening.gloss: the tone visibly opens into its brightness

techniques.code:
kc      = kfreq * koct1
kdep    = 0.45   ; depth[0.0..1.0]: how deep operator 2 drives the carrier, in CYCLES of phase
kstk    = 0.35   ; stack[0.0..1.0]: how much operator 3 drives operator 2 -- a modulator that is
                 ;   itself modulated, which is the one thing a chain does that no number of
                 ;   parallel operators can
kfbk    = 0.25   ; feedback[0.0..1.0]: how far operator 2 modulates its OWN phase
krat    = 1.00   ; ratio[0.25..8.0]: operator 2's tuning against the note -- a whole number is
                 ;   harmonic, between them not
krhi    = 2.00   ; ratio hi[0.25..8.0]: operator 3's tuning
kdec    = 0.45   ; decay[0.0..1.0]: how long the drive holds before it falls back
kons    = 0.02   ; onset[0.002..0.6]: seconds the sidebands need to arrive
; --- an envelope PER OPERATOR, exponential to a floor and faster the higher up the
;     chain: that is what a DX7 patch does, and what one shared brightness cannot
ktau2   = 0.08 + 5.0 * kdec * kdec
ktau3   = ktau2 * 0.45
kenv2   = 0.28 + 0.72 * exp(-knote / ktau2)
kenv3   = 0.16 + 0.84 * exp(-knote / ktau3)
karr    = min(knote / kons, 1)
; --- one slow free-running swing so a held note keeps moving. Not a level wobble and not
;     vibrato: it moves how much of the spectrum the UPPER operator and the feedback are
;     responsible for. Measured at the default: 299 cents of centroid over the sustain
ksw     oscili 0.35, 0.37, giSine
ki2     = kdep * kenv2 * karr
ki3     = kstk * kenv3 * karr * (1 + ksw)
kifb    = kfbk * kenv2 * karr * (1 + 0.8 * ksw)
; --- Nyquist: the chain's top edge in units of the played pitch, each stage broadening
;     the one below it. Conservative, because scaling every index shrinks a nested
;     product faster than it shrinks this linear bound
kw3     = krhi * (1 + 6.2832 * ki3)
kw2     = krat * (1 + 6.2832 * kifb) + 6.2832 * ki2 * kw3
kroom   limit (min(sr * 0.45, 20000) / kc) - 1, 0.5, 4000
kscl    = min(1, kroom / max(kw2, 0.001))
ki2s    = ki2 * kscl
ki3s    = ki3 * kscl
kfbs    = kifb * kscl
; --- the operators. phasor + tablei IS the operator. The feedback is the AVERAGE of
;     operator 2's last TWO outputs, which is what the DX7's OPS does (MSFA fm_op.cc;
;     Shirriff on the YM21280) and is not a detail: a single-sample loop is the same
;     circuit without the one thing that keeps it from breaking into noise
a3      tablei (phasor:a(kc * krhi)), giSine, 1, 0, 1
afb2    init 0
a2      tablei (phasor:a(kc * krat)) + a3 * ki3s + afb2, giSine, 1, 0, 1
afbA    delay1 a2
afbB    delay1 afbA
afb2    = (afbA + afbB) * 0.5 * kfbs
acar    tablei (phasor:a(kc)) + a2 * ki2s, giSine, 1, 0, 1
aref    poscil 0.45, kc                     ; steady level reference
asig    balance acar, aref, 10              ; loudness held, colour free
asig    = asig * kvol1

techniques.why: drum head / tom / timpani / taiko / conga / djembe: a stretched membrane resonating, whose partials are NOT a harmonic series -- that is what makes a drum a drum; pitched = indefinite tom to definite kettledrum, spot = struck in the centre or at the rim, tension = slack and dull to tight and bright, damping = ringing open or muffled to a thud

pitched.note: how definite the pitch is. an ideal stretched membrane rings at spacings that are not whole-number multiples, so it has no clear note -- that is a tom. loading the head with air in a kettle pulls those spacings towards whole numbers until a real pitch appears -- that is a timpani. this is the deepest thing about the instrument, not a tuning offset: the played pitch itself never changes here, only whether the drum sounds like it HAS one.

tom.gloss: no clear note, just a low woody thump

mixed.gloss: a note starts to emerge from the thump

timpani.gloss: a real singing pitch, a tuned kettledrum

strikepos.note: where the head is struck. dead centre wakes only the modes that breathe evenly across the whole skin, which is round and deep; nearer the rim wakes the ones that ripple around it, which is thinner, harder and more sharply coloured. a real player uses this constantly.

tension.note: how tightly the head is stretched, heard as which partials carry the sound rather than as pitch. slack leaves only the lowest ones and sounds dull and floppy; tight brings the upper ones up and sounds bright and taut.

damping.note: how freely the head is allowed to ring, as with a hand or a felt ring on the skin. open leaves narrow clear resonances that sing; muffled broadens them until the drum reads as a thud with a colour rather than a tone.

muffled.gloss: dead and thuddy, a cloth on the skin

techniques.why: gong / tam-tam / anvil / singing bowl / metallic percussion: two phase-modulation operators standing on the (3,0) and (4,0) modes Chladni's law predicts for a free circular plate, driving one carrier and a second carrier a few Hz above it. The exponent of that law is the instrument's main axis, so the metal runs from a tight nearly-pitched body to a wide plate with no note left; each mode has its own decay, so the attack is bright and the tail is not.

stretch.note: how far the metal's modes stand off a harmonic series. This is not a free number: it is the exponent p of Chladni's law, f = C(m+2n)^p, and the two operators are placed at the (3,0) and (4,0) modes it predicts. The range is the published one for cymbals, handbells and church bells. Low is a tight metal that still carries the note; high is a wide plate whose partials no longer add up to a pitch.

tight.gloss: the modes closest together: a small, nearly-pitched metal

bell.gloss: the middle of the published range: struck bell, the note still there

plate.gloss: a flat circular plate, the value the law gives for one: gong

wide.gloss: the top of the published range: the partials furthest apart, no note left

index.note: how hard the two modes are driven -- how many partials the metal carries. Low leaves the note almost bare; high fills the spectrum between the modes and loosens the pitch, because a deep index empties the carrier itself.

struck softly.gloss: barely driven: the note with a trace of metal on it

struck.gloss: an ordinary strike, the modes clearly there

struck hard.gloss: hard: the spectrum fills in between the modes

hammered.gloss: hammered, the pitch beginning to loosen

crashed.gloss: everything the two modes can put out

damping.note: how much faster a mode dies for standing higher. Kirchhoff's plate equation has two loss terms: one that damps every mode alike -- that is `ring` -- and one that grows with the mode's frequency. This is the second one. At zero the metal is damped evenly and keeps its colour for as long as the note lasts; turned up, the modes the law puts furthest out go first, and what is left is the plain low body. A held note keeps driving the plate, so a mode that dies faster also stands lower the whole way through -- this is not only an attack shape.

even.gloss: no frequency-dependent loss at all: every mode falls at the same rate and the metal holds its colour to the end of the note

metal.gloss: the default: the (4,0) mode dies about twice as fast as the body and stands about half as high -- an ordinary struck metal

dead top.gloss: the top is gone in a fifth of the time and sits 20 dB down: the low body alone, still ringing

ring.note: how long the drive holds before the metal darkens. Low collapses to a plain body almost at once; high stays lit deep into the note. The host owns when the note stops -- this is the colour, not the loudness.

quick.gloss: the metal darkens almost at once

long.gloss: stays lit well into the note

beat.note: how fast the two struck bodies swell against each other. NOT a detune: the offset is a fraction of a Hertz and you never hear it as pitch, you hear the two bodies going in and out of step -- BJ, 2026-07-31, on the name it used to carry: „das ist kein detune“. The swell has to be SLOW: the n-th partial swells n times as fast as the first, so an offset near 1 Hz makes the third partial pulse almost four times a second, which he heard as hectic. The whole axis stays under 0.5 Hz. At zero the two lock and the body stands still -- the static escape, and about 2.7 dB louder, because two bodies in step add where two bodies beating do not.

locked.gloss: the two bodies in step: one still body, and the loudest setting

slow.gloss: 0.2 Hz: one swell every five seconds

wide.gloss: 0.43 Hz: the fastest swell this body offers

techniques.code:
kc      = kfreq * koct1
kidx    = 0.53   ; index[0.0..1.0]: how hard the two modes are driven -- how many partials the
                 ;   metal carries, and how far the pitch of the note loosens
kstr    = 1.70   ; stretch[1.40..2.40]: Chladni's exponent p in f = C(m+2n)^p. The published
                 ;   range for cymbals, handbells and church bells; about 2 is a flat circular
                 ;   plate, the gong end. Low is a tight, nearly-pitched metal
kring   = 0.56   ; ring[0.0..1.0]: how long the drive holds before the metal darkens
kdmp    = 0.35   ; damping[0.0..1.0]: how much faster the upper mode dies than the lower one
; LOUDNESS: beat
kbeat   = 0.50   ; beat[0.0..1.0]: how fast the two struck bodies swell against each other
; --- the two ratios are COMPUTED from the law, not chosen. Modes (2,0) (3,0) (4,0) of a
;     free circular plate have (m+2n) = 2, 3, 4, so f_k / f_2 = (k/2)^p
kr2     = pow(1.5, kstr)         ; operator 2 stands ON the (3,0) mode
kr3     = pow(2.0, kstr)         ; operator 3 stands ON the (4,0) mode
; --- Kirchhoff's plate equation carries TWO loss terms (Schaefer, Werner & Rabenstein,
;     "Physical Modeling of Vibrating Plates", DAGA 2019 Rostock, 299-302, eq. 1). d1 is
;     frequency-independent and "leads to a uniform damping for all oscillation modes" --
;     that is `ring`. d3 scales with the squared wavenumber, and since the squared
;     wavenumber goes with the mode's FREQUENCY (eq. 15), the decay rate of eq. 14 is
;     affine in the mode ratio: the higher a mode stands, the faster it dies. d3 is
;     `damping`. A held note keeps driving the plate, and a driven damped mode settles at
;     drive/rate -- so a mode that dies q times faster also STANDS q times lower. That is
;     the steady state of the same equation, not a number fitted to a result.
ktau    = 0.15 + 6.0 * kring * kring
kd3     = 3.0 * kdmp * kdmp
kq2     = 1 + kd3 * (kr2 - 1)               ; mode (3,0) decays this many times faster
kq3     = 1 + kd3 * (kr3 - 1)               ; mode (4,0), standing higher, faster still
kf2     = 0.30 / kq2                        ; and sits that much lower while driven
kf3     = 0.30 / kq3
kenv2   = kf2 + (1 - kf2) * exp(-knote * kq2 / ktau)
kenv3   = kf3 + (1 - kf3) * exp(-knote * kq3 / ktau)
ksw     oscili 0.30, 0.31, giSine   ; slow, free-running: which mode carries the metal
ki2     = kidx * 0.60 * kenv2 * (1 - ksw)
ki3     = kidx * 0.42 * kenv3 * (1 + ksw)
; --- Nyquist, Carson's rule per operator and summed -- both modulators arrive on ONE carrier
;     phase, so the deviation that counts is their SUM and the room is shared. `fm3` records
;     what happens otherwise: "bounding each operator as if it were alone is what put a
;     49 kHz sideband on a 440 Hz note". What is reserved is what an operator
;     can EVER ask for -- `index` at the top of its range, envelope at 1, ksw at its peak --
;     never what it is asking for right now. A guard that divides by the live index divides
;     the envelope and the axis straight back out: every common factor of ki2 and ki3
;     cancels against kneed, and where the guard bites, `ring`, `damping` and `index` stop
;     doing anything at all. Measured 2026-07-31 before this line was written: at 1760 Hz,
;     stretch 2.4, damping 0, three `ring` settings rendered BIT-IDENTICAL and moves() went
;     False. `fm3` already reserves from an operator's peak for this reason. kroom has a
;     FLOOR and not a zero, because a body whose room reaches zero is a bare sine with every
;     axis dead. DECLARED LIMIT, measured 2026-07-31 and shared with `fm3`: the 20000 ceiling
;     dates from when the page and the plugin still ran at 1x, and against it this pot is
;     already at its floor by A7 -- at 3520 Hz the body is close to a sine and its colour
;     travels 9 Hz, under the movement gate. Every register up to and including A6 moves.
kpk2    = 0.60 * 1.30
kpk3    = 0.42 * 1.30
kroom   limit (min(sr * 0.45, 20000) / kc) - 1 - kr2 - kr3, 0.5, 4000
kneed   = 6.2832 * (kpk2 * kr2 + kpk3 * kr3)
kscl    = min(1, kroom / max(kneed, 0.001))  ; one factor for both, so their balance holds
ki2s    = ki2 * kscl
ki3s    = ki3 * kscl
; --- two modulators on one carrier's phase, and a second carrier a few Hz above, so the
;     pair beats the way two struck metal bodies do
am2     poscil ki2s, kc * kr2, giSine
am3     poscil ki3s, kc * kr3, giSine
kbea    = 0.5 * kbeat           ; Hz, so the SLOWEST partial beats at kbea and the
                                ;   n-th at n*kbea -- which is why this has to stay well
                                ;   under 1 Hz: at 1.3 Hz the third partial beat 3.9 times
                                ;   a second and BJ heard it as hectic (2026-07-31)
acr1    tablei (phasor:a(kc)) + am2 + am3, giSine, 1, 0, 1
acr2    tablei (phasor:a(kc + kbea)) + am2 + am3, giSine, 1, 0, 1
asum    = acr1 * 0.60 + acr2 * 0.40
aref    poscil 0.45, kc                     ; steady level reference
; The level stage sees ONE voice, not the pair. A follower fast enough for the spectral
; onset (10 Hz) is by definition fast enough to FLATTEN a beat slower than that, and at
; ihp=1 it still swallows anything under a Hz -- docs/LCO_CONCEPT.md l.173 records that
; `fm_bell`'s ihp=1 "exists to protect its doublet beat", and this body's beat is slower

techniques.why: plucked or bowed string / guitar / harp / koto / pizzicato / violin / cello: ONE real string, set going and then left to ring -- NOT the ensemble string machine (that is `strings`, detuned saws) and NOT the plucked-string spectrum without the pluck (that is `harpsichord`, gbuzz choirs). The string is a comb resonator tuned to the played pitch. It has to be fed the whole time so a held note stands and the synth's own envelope does the striking -- but the feed arrives as scattered, time-smeared touches and the ring is kept long, so what is heard is the string and not what is driving it. A continuous wall of noise into the same resonator is audibly an electric string driver: aggressive and restless. Its top dies away after the attack the way a real string loses its brilliance -- twice over, fast for the first instant and slowly for the whole ring. IF THE PROMPT WANTS A PLUCK THAT IS ALLOWED TO DIE -- struck once and left to ring down under the key -- this entry cannot do it, because it is fed the whole time on purpose; `plucked_wire` is the one, a real Karplus-Strong wire with nothing driving it after the pluck. Choose between them from what the prompt asks for. bow = plucked with a pick to drawn with a bow, pick = where the string is set going, from right at the bridge to at the middle, damp = left ringing to stopped under the hand
techniques.code:
kstr    limit kfreq * koct1, 20, 12000
kfast   = exp(-knote * 20.00)                  ; the first instant's brilliance goes at once
kslow   = exp(-knote * 0.328)                  ; and the string keeps losing its top all the while
kbrth   poscil 0.353, 0.447                ; the hand behind it is never quite steady
kcut    limit 775.0 * (1 + 2.58 * kfast) * (1 + 4.06 * kslow) * (1 + kbrth), 60, 18000
aexd    dust 1.0, 736.2                        ; the drive arrives as separate touches, not as
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.1100, 0.00710                ;   a wall of noise -- a wall is an electric
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0820, 0.00470                ;   string driver, not a played string. Each
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0640, 0.00310                ;   touch is then smeared out in time so none
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0480, 0.00190                ;   of them arrives as a click. Allpasses
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0340, 0.00113                ;   spread WITHOUT darkening; a lowpass here
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0260, 0.00079                ;   buries the instrument's own colour
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0200, 0.00053
aexd    alpass aexd, 0.0160, 0.00037
aexb    tone aexd, kcut
apik    vdelay aexb, (0.1850 / kstr) * 1000, 60
aexc    = aexb - apik
astr    streson aexc, kstr, 0.9884
aref    poscil 0.35, 400                          ; a fixed-loudness yardstick: how scattered the
abal    balance astr, aref                        ; drive is must not change how loud the tone is
asig    = abal * 0.85

bow.note: how the string is set going, and that is the whole difference between a guitar and a cello. A pick or a fingernail lets go in an instant, so everything in the string is woken at once and the sound arrives bright and then falls away. A bow never lets go: the hair grabs and slips and grabs again, feeding the string the whole time, so the top is rubbed off but nothing dies -- the tone stands and breathes instead. In the code this is how DENSELY the drive arrives: separate touches at the plucked end, a steady draw at the bowed one. Measured across the axis the colour travels from 4812 Hz down to 3463 Hz while how sharply the string rings does not change (34.3 -> 33.6 dB) and the loudness moves 0.04 dB.

plucked.gloss: picked and let go: bright at the front, then darkening

bowed.gloss: drawn with a bow: standing, breathing, the top rubbed off

pick.note: where along its length the string is set going. This is not a tone control, it is geometry: a string cannot be given any energy at a harmonic whose still point falls exactly where you touch it, so that harmonic is simply missing. Right by the bridge only the very high ones are lost and the sound is thin, hard and nasal; at the middle every even harmonic is gone at once and the sound goes hollow and woody, a clarinet made of string. Measured at the middle: harmonics 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 all drop about 30 dB, which is the real thing and not an effect. Loudness moves 0.01 dB across the axis.

bridge.gloss: played hard by the bridge: thin, wiry, nasal

middle.gloss: over the middle: hollow and woody, the even harmonics gone

damp.note: how freely the string is allowed to ring, as with the flat of the hand laid on it. Open, the resonances are narrow and the string sings a clear note; stopped, they broaden and the string reads as a knock with a colour rather than a pitch. It never stops ringing altogether -- a string whose resonance is let go stops sounding like a string at all and starts sounding like the thing driving it. Measured as how far the sound between the harmonics sits below the harmonics themselves: 38.5 dB open, 29.7 dB stopped, with the colour (4040 -> 4038 Hz) and the loudness (0.03 dB) both staying where they were.

open.gloss: left to ring, a clear singing note

damped.gloss: a hand resting on it, controlled

muted.gloss: palm-muted: a knock with a colour, barely a pitch

techniques.why: a wire under tension, plucked once and then left alone: the note is made by the pluck and nothing feeds it afterwards, so it rings and dies the way a real wire does -- long and singing at the bottom of the keyboard, a short bright tick at the top. This is NOT `string`, which is a comb resonator fed the whole time so that a held note stands; it is the other thing, an actual travelling wave in a wire, and it is the only entry in the library that fades by itself. Karplus-Strong with the Jaffe-Smith extensions (David A. Jaffe and Julius O. Smith, 'Extensions of the Karplus-Strong Plucked-String Algorithm', Computer Music Journal 7(2), 1983), as Csound's `wgpluck2` implements it: two delay rails with a one-pole reflection filter standing in for the bridge. THREE THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE REACHING FOR IT. (1) IT TAKES THE KEY AT THE START OF THE NOTE AND THEN HOLDS IT. `wgpluck2` reads its frequency at i-rate, so the `reinit` on `ktrig` in the code is what makes it play the note at all -- and glide, pitch bend, vibrato and everything else on the pitch bus do not reach it once the note has begun. A legato slide leaves the wire at the pitch it was plucked at. A note that has to bend needs a pitch-following body beside it via `+`. (2) IT DECAYS, and how fast depends steeply on the pitch. Measured at the oscillator's default 4x oversampling, time to fall 20 dB: at refl 0.70 a note at 110 and 220 Hz has still not dropped 20 dB after 25 seconds, 440 Hz takes 4.4 s and 880 Hz 0.54 s; at refl 0.85 that is 8.5 s at 220, 1.05 s at 440 and 0.14 s at 880. So a long held note in the top octave will have gone silent by itself while the key is still down. That is the wire, not a fault -- but it is why this entry does not answer a prompt that asks for a sustained tone. The ring length also follows the LRO's oversampling setting, and steeply: at 1x that same 440 Hz note is down in 0.18 s where 4x gives 2.3 s. The model grows its delay line by whole periods until it holds at least 512 samples and rescales the reflection to match, so a shorter line -- a lower rate or a higher note -- ends up with a lossier bridge. It cannot be undone from outside: unwinding that rescaling would need a reflection below zero, which the model does not accept. Every figure here is at the default. (3) IT PLAYS SLIGHTLY FLAT, more so the higher the note and the higher refl. The bridge filter's pole is refl itself, so raising it adds delay to the loop, and the loop's length is the pitch; the delay line is also truncated to whole samples, which bites harder the shorter it is. Measured across the axis: within 4 cents at 110 and 220 Hz, within 18 at 440, and up to 44 cents flat at 880. The mechanism is read off the model's own source; the size of it is not derived, it is declared, and that is why the axis stops at 0.85. ABOVE THE AXIS IS COLOUR, NOT A NOTE. refl 0.90 to 0.98 is a different thing altogether: at 0.98 the sound is gone in 0.17 s at 220 Hz and sits 91 cents flat there, 172 cents at 440. What is left is a crackle, a small dry transient. Worth having -- layered under a pitched body with `+`, never asked to carry the pitch. THE PICKUP POINT IS THE SECOND AXIS. `pick` is where along the wire the sound is heard, and it is real geometry: a harmonic whose still point falls on that spot is simply missing. At 220 Hz, read over the first half-second because the note is already dying after that, the second harmonic runs from -7.0 dB below the fundamental at 0.25 to -11.0 at 0.35, and the third drops into a 68 dB hole at 0.33 -- wiry, then reedy, then round. It moves the LEVEL as well, and the body declares that instead of hiding it (`; LOUDNESS: pick`): across the axis the peak falls 1.25 dB while the note's settled energy RISES 1.75, in opposite directions, and the peak moves by the same amount at every register (-1.24 to -1.25 dB from 55 to 1760 Hz). What travels is the distance between them -- the peak sits 9.7 dB above the settled level at 0.25 and 6.7 dB at 0.35 -- because the wave is spiky near the end of the wire and smooth further along. That is a pluck being a transient, not a volume control, and it is the case §4 stopped judging by threshold on 2026-07-27. Both figures are `lco_measure`'s own peak and rms at the oscillator's default 4x. THE AXIS STOPS AT 0.35 FOR MOVEMENT, NOT FOR LOUDNESS. Raising the pickup damps the colour's travel over the note (46 Hz at 0.25, 20 at 0.35, 16 at 0.37), and at 0.37 combined with the shortest ring (refl 0.85) the body stands still outright when the LRO is run at 1x oversampling. 0.35 is the last point that still moves at every refl and every oversampling setting. Beyond it: at 0.50 the colour stands still at 55, 110 and 220 Hz, and past 0.50 nothing is new -- that is the middle of the wire and everything beyond mirrors what came before, 0.80 measuring within 3 dB of 0.20 over the first six partials. The middle itself, 0.50, kills the even harmonics outright (second harmonic 43 dB down at the attack) and stands still: a striking sound, and a deliberate one -- set it by hand, outside the axis. TWO NOTES ON THE CODE. There is deliberately NO `dcblock`: `wgpluck2` produces no DC worth blocking here (0.05 % of rms at worst), while `dcblock2`'s corner scales with the sample rate, so at the oscillator's 4x it becomes an ~800 Hz highpass that takes 23 dB out of a note at 110 Hz -- it destroys exactly the low end this body is good at. And `PLUCKWIRE:` is a LABEL, which cannot be indexed the way this library's variable names are: a second copy of this body in the same instrument must be given a different label. IF THE PROMPT WANTS A PLUCKED SOUND THAT STANDS while the key is held, this is the wrong entry and `string` is the right one -- same family, fed continuously, so a held note does not die. Choose between them from what the prompt asks for. refl = how long it rings.

refl.note: how long the wire rings on after the pluck. Low is the long one: at 0.70 a note below about 300 Hz simply does not stop inside the note, and 440 Hz takes 4.4 s to fall 20 dB; at 0.85 that same 440 Hz is down in 1.05 s and 880 Hz in 0.14 s. So the axis runs from a wire left ringing to a short dry pluck, and it shortens much faster the higher you play. It also detunes: the note goes flat as the axis rises, measured +3.2 down to -3.9 cents at 220 Hz across the window and -4.0 to -18.2 at 440. That is what stops the axis at 0.85 rather than at 0.98, where the model still runs but the pitch is no longer the played one -- that region is a crackle, not a note, and the entry text says how to use it. The two loudness meters disagree on this axis and the difference IS the parameter: the attack does not move at all (peak spread 0.0 dB at 110, 220 and 440 Hz), while the note's total energy falls -- 0.5 dB at 110 Hz, 2.9 at 220, 6.1 at 440 -- because a shorter ring simply holds less of it. It is not a fader; it is the ring length being what it says.

ringing.gloss: left to ring: below 300 Hz it never stops inside the note

plucked.gloss: an ordinary pluck, ringing but clearly dying

dry.gloss: short and dry, and already a few cents flat

pick.note: where along the wire the sound is picked up, as a fraction of its length. A harmonic with a node at that point is cancelled, so the axis runs wiry (near the end, all harmonics present and the second only 7 dB down at the attack) through hollow (0.33, where the third harmonic falls into a 68 dB hole) to round. It is a TIMBRE axis that also moves the level, declared as such in the body: from 0.25 to 0.35 the peak falls 1.25 dB while the four-second energy rises 1.75, so neither meter alone is 'the loudness' -- what moves is the distance between them, 9.7 dB down to 6.7. The axis ends at 0.35 because the colour's travel over the note thins out as the pickup rises (46 Hz at 0.25, 20 at 0.35) and at 0.37 with the shortest ring the body stops moving altogether at 1x oversampling; past 0.50 the wire mirrors itself.

wiry.gloss: near the end of the wire: spiky, all harmonics, hard attack

hollow.gloss: the third harmonic cancelled -- reedy, a little nasal

round.gloss: smoother and softer-edged, the last point that still moves at every refl

techniques.why: supersaw / hypersaw -- the trance and rave lead, and the JP-8000's string pads. Seven sawtooth oscillators, one of them the played note and six standing off it. This is a DIGITAL oscillator and that is the whole reason it is its own entry: the saws are deliberately not band limited, so they alias, and Szabo names that fold-back as one of the four things every other emulation misses -- it is what makes the sound airy. Built from Adam Szabo, `How to Emulate the Super Saw`, BSc thesis, KTH Stockholm 2010 (TRITA-CSC-E 2010:131), which measured a Roland JP-8000 and JP-8080: the detune offsets (table 1), the 11th degree detune curve (fig 7), the two mix curves (fig 11), the pitch-tracking high pass on the first harmonic (fig 14/15) and the free-running random phases (fig 18-21). `detune` and `mix` are the machine's own two knobs.
techniques.code:
kdetune = 0.50    ; detune [0..1]: how far the six side saws stand off the centre one
kmix    = 0.75    ; mix [0..1]: the six against the centre; they are equal at 0.75

kknob   limit kdetune, 0, 1                    ; Szabo 2010 fig 7: the JP-8000's detune knob
kpoly   = 10028.7312891634                     ;   is NOT proportional. An 11th degree fit
kpoly   = kpoly * kknob - 50818.8652045924     ;   through 17 measured points, by Horner --
kpoly   = kpoly * kknob + 111363.4808729368    ;   nearly flat to 0.5, steep after 0.9, so
kpoly   = kpoly * kknob - 138150.6761080548    ;   most of the knob is fine tuning and only
kpoly   = kpoly * kknob + 106649.6679158292    ;   the top of it spreads wide
kpoly   = kpoly * kknob - 53046.9642751875
kpoly   = kpoly * kknob + 17019.9518580080
kpoly   = kpoly * kknob - 3425.0836591318
kpoly   = kpoly * kknob + 404.2703938388
kpoly   = kpoly * kknob - 24.1878824391
kpoly   = kpoly * kknob + 0.6717417634
kspread limit kpoly * kknob + 0.0030115596, 0, 1

kf0     = kfreq * koct1                        ; Szabo 2010 table 1: the offsets are not
kfa     = kf0 * (1 - 0.11002313 * kspread)     ;   symmetric and not evenly spaced; the
kfb     = kf0 * (1 - 0.06288439 * kspread)     ;   centre saw is never detuned at all
kfc     = kf0 * (1 - 0.01952356 * kspread)
kfd     = kf0 * (1 + 0.01991221 * kspread)
kfe     = kf0 * (1 + 0.06216538 * kspread)
kff     = kf0 * (1 + 0.10745242 * kspread)

ipa     = rnd(1)                               ; free running: every note trigger gives each
ipb     = rnd(1)                               ;   saw a fresh phase, so no two notes have
ipc     = rnd(1)                               ;   the same waveform. Szabo 2010 fig 18-21:
ipd     = rnd(1)                               ;   resetting them to a fixed phase makes the
ipe     = rnd(1)                               ;   attacks flange identically every time,
ipf     = rnd(1)                               ;   and modulating them adds artefacts

detune.note: how far the six side saws stand off the centre one. The knob is not proportional: Szabo fitted an 11th degree polynomial through 17 measured settings, and it stays nearly flat to 0.5, steepens, then rises drastically after 0.9. So most of the travel is fine tuning -- measured on the outermost saw at 220 Hz: +0.6 cents at 0, +8.7 at 0.25, +18.1 at 0.5, +44.5 at 0.75, +176.7 at 1.0. The offsets are not symmetric and the centre saw is never detuned at all. The beating between the seven is the movement of this body: 2.3 dB at 0, 9.5 dB at 0.5.

tight.gloss: all seven on the note; one thick saw, barely moving

classic.gloss: +18 cents on the outer saw -- the pad and string spread

wide.gloss: +177 cents, close to a chord; the screaming lead end

mix.note: the six side saws against the centre one. Turning it up pulls the centre saw DOWN in a straight line while the six come up in a parabola; they meet at 0.75, not at the maximum the JP-8000 manual claims. Both curves are Szabo's fits to the measured amplitudes. Level follows: 3.8 dB from 0 to 0.75, because six saws add incoherently where one does not.

centred.gloss: the six are almost silent -- a single aliasing saw

even.gloss: all seven at the same level, where they were measured to meet

hollow.gloss: the centre pulled under the six; the note itself recedes

techniques.why: analogue oscillator / vco / dco / minimoog / juno / prophet: ONE waveform generator with every control the shape needs. `wave` picks between two vco2 generators -- the ramp one and the pulse one -- and `width` is the SAME position on both: the fraction of the period spent in the first phase, symmetric at 0.5. So a waveform is a pair of numbers, not a name: a triangle is wave 0 with width 0.5, a saw wave 0 with width near either end, a square wave 1 with width 0.5, a narrow pulse wave 1 with width 0.12. The width is a modulation DESTINATION -- whatever writes it, an LFO, an envelope, a hand, is pulse width modulation, and the measure of that movement is the interval of widths it covers. `finetune` shifts the pitch in cents so several layers can be detuned against each other; `drive` crossfades into a band-limited asymmetric clipper, which puts even harmonics into a triangle or a pulse that had none and redraws a saw that already had every one; `age` is component drift, and it is the axis between the two kinds of machine in that list: at 0 nothing drifts and this is a DCO, the Juno's digitally clocked pitch, while the drift itself is what a VCO does -- the Minimoog, the Prophet. Level holds to 0.13 dB across `drive` and six registers; across `width` it does not, and must not -- see that parameter.

wave.note: which of the two generators is heard: 0 the ramp one (vco2 imode 4), 1 the pulse one (imode 2), and between them the two are crossfaded. Both read `width` as the same fourth argument, so this control does not name a waveform on its own -- it picks the family and `width` picks the position in it. Measured at 220 Hz with the width at its symmetric 0.5: centroid 675 Hz on the ramp generator (a triangle) against 5620 on the pulse one (a square); at width 0.02 the ramp generator reads 2180 (a saw).

ramp.gloss: the triangle/saw generator -- `width` sets where the ramp breaks

pulse.gloss: the square/pulse generator -- `width` sets the duty

width.note: the fraction of one period spent in the first phase -- rising on the ramp generator, high on the pulse generator -- and it is the same argument to vco2 in both cases. 0.5 is the symmetric one on either: a triangle, a square. There every even harmonic cancels -- odd/even measured 131.3 dB on the ramp generator and 96.5 on the pulse one -- because the amplitudes carry |sin(pi*n*w)| on both (over n on the pulse, over n^2 on the ramp -- the pulse is the derivative of the asymmetric triangle, which is one power of n). Away from 0.5 the even harmonics come in and the nth is cancelled wherever n*w is a whole number. w and 1-w are the same magnitude spectrum, so 0.12 and 0.88 sound alike: measured on the pulse generator with `age` at 0, odd/even 1.6 dB against 1.6 and centroids 4317.1 against 4317.4 Hz. On the PULSE generator a width off 0.5 is also quieter, because the DC it carries, A*(2w-1), is taken out and a narrow pulse is mostly that -- measured 3.77 dB down at 0.12 against 0.5 and 11.28 at 0.02, where rms 2A*sqrt(w(1-w)) predicts 3.74 and 11.06 -- and that is the sound of the thing, not a fault to correct. On the RAMP generator there is no such term: its rms is 1/sqrt(3) at every width -- measured -9.21 dB at 0.02, 0.12, 0.5, 0.88 and 0.98 alike -- so there the same number is colour alone.

end.gloss: the far end: a sawtooth on the ramp generator, a sliver of a pulse on the other

narrow.gloss: well off symmetric -- thin and nasal, and on the pulse generator quieter

symmetric.gloss: odd harmonics only, on either generator: a triangle, a square

wide.gloss: the mirror of narrow -- same spectrum, same level

finetune.note: cents off the played note, so two or three layers of this oscillator can be detuned against each other -- the octave knobs the player has (koct1/2/3) move in octaves and cannot do it. Beating between two layers a few cents apart is what makes a sound thick; that thickness is composed from layers here and is not a knob on one oscillator. Measured: -25 asked gives -25 heard.

flat.gloss: a slow beat against a layer at zero

sharp.gloss: the same beat the other way

drive.note: how far the oscillator is crossfaded into a band-limited asymmetric clipper (`distort1`). The band limit is the point of it: fed the FULL saw a memoryless shaper can only REDRAW the wave -- for a ramp input the output waveform IS the transfer curve, and a saw already carries every harmonic at 1/n, so measured over the whole bounded region of `distort1` every setting takes every partial DOWN at equal loudness. Behind a band limit the shaper regenerates a top instead, which is where a real overdrive's clipper sits. The asymmetry is the other half: `tanh` is an ODD function and can never put an even harmonic into a waveform that has none -- on the triangle it lifts only the odd partials and leaves even/odd at 0.000, where `kshape2` -0.4 takes it to 0.255, and the pulse from 0.000 to 0.161. On the saw, which already has every harmonic, nothing is added and the drive only redraws: even/odd 0.664 to 0.226, centroid 2005 to 2837 Hz. So what this control does depends on the waveform, and it does most where the wave is emptiest. Level holds to 0.13 dB across the axis and six registers.

warm.gloss: a third of the way into the clipper

hot.gloss: all the way in -- the clipper alone

age.note: how far the components have drifted: a slow pitch wander, a jitter on the duty, and a slow level wobble, each scaled by this one value and each at its own unrelated rate so they never lock. At 0 the oscillator is mathematically exact and sounds it: that setting is a DCO and not a VCO -- rock-stable digital pitch is the thing a DCO was built to have. Every voice enters the drift at a different phase, so a chord does not wander in lockstep.

dco.gloss: no drift at all. This is what a DCO IS: the pitch comes off a divider rather than out of a VCO's temperature-dependent core, so it does not move. BJ named this anchor (2026-07-30) — and the entry already answers to `juno`, which is one.

techniques.code:
; LOUDNESS: width
; LOUDNESS: wave
; the pulse generator's level follows its width: what is left once the DC A*(2w-1)
; is taken out is 2A*sqrt(w(1-w)) -- 3.77 dB down at 0.12 and 11.28 at 0.02. So
; `width` moves the level on that generator, and `wave`, which decides how much of
; it is heard, carries that with it. The ramp generator has no such term: rms
; 1/sqrt(3) at every width. A pulse gets quieter the narrower it gets, and that IS
; pulse width modulation (BJ 2026-07-28, LCO_CONCEPT.md section 4).
kwave   = 0.00    ; wave [0..1]: which generator -- 0 the ramp, 1 the pulse
kwidth  = 0.02    ; width [0.02..0.98]: the fraction of the period spent in the first phase
kfinetune = 0.00  ; finetune [-50..50]: cents off the played note
kdrive  = 0.00    ; drive [0..1]: mixed into a band-limited asymmetric clipper
kage    = 0.35    ; age [0..1]: component drift -- pitch, width and level wobble

ivph    = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)          ; each voice enters the drift elsewhere
kdrf    poscil 0.007 * kage, 0.043 + 0.0037 * ivoice, giSine, ivph
kjit    poscil 0.012 * kage, 0.057             ; age: width jitter
klvl    oscili 0.030 * kage, 0.7               ; age: level wobble
kf0     = (kfreq * koct1) * (2 ^ (kfinetune / 1200)) * (1 + kdrf)

kfold   = kwidth + kjit                        ; ONE width, and both generators read it
kdw     limit abs(kfold - 2 * round(kfold * 0.5)), 0.01, 0.99
                                               ; the clamp sits OUTSIDE the axis on
                                               ;   purpose. At 0.02 it would sit on
                                               ;   the width's own end and eat the
                                               ;   negative half of `kjit` there --
                                               ;   the drift would stop at exactly
                                               ;   the setting the entry ships. 0.01
                                               ;   and 0.99 is what Csound asks for.
                                               ; it FOLDS at 0 and 1 rather than wrapping:
                                               ;   w and 1-w are the same spectrum, so the
                                               ;   sound travels the same path either way,
                                               ;   but a wrap makes vco2 jump across its
                                               ;   own table discontinuity and emit a lone
                                               ;   one-sample spike. Measured over 8 s at
                                               ;   full depth: 15 wrapping, 0 folding.
aramp   vco2 0.6, kf0, 4, kdw                  ; ramp: 0.5 a triangle, either end a saw
apuls   vco2 0.6, kf0, 2, kdw                  ; pulse: 0.5 a square, either end narrow
apuls   = apuls - 0.6 * (2 * kdw - 1)          ; a width off 0.5 carries DC A*(2w-1), and
                                               ;   taking it out leaves the pulse quieter
                                               ;   the narrower it is -- 3.77 dB at 0.12.
                                               ;   The ramp has no such term: rms 1/sqrt(3)
                                               ;   at every width, colour alone.
aosc    = aramp * (1 - kwave) + apuls * kwave

apre    tone aosc, kfreq * koct1 * 5.0         ; the shaper never sees the whole
                                               ;   oscillator, and the band limit tracks
                                               ;   the note. Fed a FULL saw a memoryless
                                               ;   shaper can only REDRAW it: for a ramp
                                               ;   input the output waveform IS the
                                               ;   transfer curve, and a saw already
                                               ;   carries every harmonic at 1/n, so at
                                               ;   equal loudness there is nothing left to
                                               ;   add -- measured over the whole bounded
                                               ;   region of distort1, on the raw saw
                                               ;   EVERY setting takes EVERY partial down.
                                               ;   Behind a band limit it regenerates a
                                               ;   top instead, which is where a real
                                               ;   overdrive's clipper sits.
adst    distort1 apre, 16, 1, 0, -0.4, 2       ; imode 2: the shapes are relative to the
                                               ;   pregain, and at shape1 = shape2 = 0
                                               ;   distort1 IS tanh(pregain * x). tanh is
                                               ;   an ODD function -- its even part is
                                               ;   identically zero -- so it can never put
                                               ;   an even harmonic into a waveform that
                                               ;   has none: on the triangle it lifts the
                                               ;   odd partials and leaves even/odd at
                                               ;   0.000. kshape2 -0.4 curves the negative
                                               ;   half differently from the positive one
                                               ;   and takes it to 0.255.
adst    balance adst, aosc, 1                  ; ONE bright version, matched to the clean
amix    = aosc * (1 - kdrive) + adst * kdrive  ;   one ONCE, then crossfaded -- so the
                                               ;   drive amount never moves a gain into
                                               ;   the shaper.
adrv    balance amix, aosc, 1                  ; the two ends correlate 0.77, so no fixed
                                               ;   crossfade law holds the level between
                                               ;   them: linear dips 0.84 dB in the middle
                                               ;   of the knob, equal power bumps 2.19.
                                               ;   The mix is held instead, at a 1 Hz
                                               ;   corner -- `balance`'s 10 Hz default
                                               ;   ripples at 110 Hz, which at 55 Hz IS
                                               ;   the second harmonic, and that is what
                                               ;   made the old drive sound different in
                                               ;   the bass. kdrive is a knob, not an LFO,
                                               ;   so nothing fast is being chased.
asig    = adrv * (1 + klvl)

techniques.why: air blown across the mouth of a bottle: a wide, soft, almost noteless tone with only two or three partials over the breath, and it stands as long as it is blown. Built from Csound's waveguide clarinet bore with its breath at the documented ceiling, where the reed stops reading as a reed and what is left is air over an opening; the bore's upper colour is then cut back to how open the blow sounds. NOT the reed instrument (`clarinet`) and not a struck vessel. blow = from a dull hoot with barely more than the fundamental, through the two spots that read as a real blown bottle, up to where the tube saturates and nothing further is added.
techniques.code:
kdrift  oscili 0.16, 0.07, giSine        ; the blow is never quite steady
kblow   = 0.42 + kdrift
kmult   = 1.2 * (10 ^ kblow)                ; how far up the bore's colour is let through
asig    wgclar 0.5, kfreq * koct1, -0.3, 0.1, 0.1, 0.5, 5.735, 0, giSine, 30
                                            ; kngain at its documented ceiling (0.5): at the top
                                            ; of that axis the reed stops being a reed and the
                                            ; tube reads as air across the mouth of a bottle.
                                            ; the -0.3 is `kstiff` and is INERT -- measured
                                            ; bit-identical from -0.9 to 0.0 in this build, so
                                            ; never put a control on it.
                                            ; kvamp is 0: the model's own vibrato stays off.
asig    butterlp asig, kfreq * koct1 * kmult
asig    = asig * 1.45 * kvol1

blow.note: how far up the bore's own colour is let through, and with it how hard the blowing reads. measured over the whole range: the spectral centroid travels 456 -> 2188 Hz and the number of audible partials goes 2 -> 6, while the loudness moves only 2.3 dB, so this is a colour control and not a volume one. above the top the tube saturates: cutting at 12, 20 or 30 times the pitch gives the same file to three decimal places.

hooted.gloss: a dull hoot, barely more than the fundamental

open bottle.gloss: the same bottle blown more openly

saturated.gloss: as open as the tube goes; nothing more is added

techniques.why: a metal body held ringing by moving air rather than struck: three modes at stretched, non-whole-number spacings, driven continuously by filtered noise whose brightness keeps travelling, so the body never settles and a held note stands. Enigmatic rather than like any named instrument -- machine-room, industrial. Same modal filter bank as `struck_bar` and `cymbal`, but a different body: those are tuned bars and cymbals with whole-number-ish or dense spacings, this one is deliberately stretched and its character comes from the drive moving. stretch = from a hollow whole-number tube to a wide stretched bell. drive = how bright the air working the body is.

kstr    = 0.475                             ; how far the modes are stretched off whole numbers
kr2     = 2.00 + 1.60 * kstr
kr3     = 3.00 + 5.20 * kstr
kdrv    = 0.40                              ; how bright the air driving the body is
kcen    = 600 * (11.667 ^ kdrv)
aexc    rand 0.05
kcut    oscili kcen * 0.35, 0.09, giSine     ; the drive keeps moving, so the body keeps changing
kcut    = kcen + kcut
aexc    butterlp aexc, kcut
a1      mode aexc, kfreq * koct1, 340        ; three modes, driven CONTINUOUSLY rather than struck:
a2      mode aexc, kfreq * koct1 * kr2, 260  ;   a held note stands, and the host owns the note-off
a3      mode aexc, kfreq * koct1 * kr3, 190
asig    = (a1 * 0.6 + a2 * 0.3 + a3 * 0.16) * 0.27
asig    = asig * kvol1

stretch.note: how far the two upper modes sit off whole-number multiples of the played pitch. at zero they are the 2nd and 3rd harmonic and the body reads as a hollow tube with a note; stretched, the spacings go wide and it reads as a bell or a plate with no clear note. measured: centroid 363 -> 532 Hz across the axis with the loudness holding inside 0.2 dB. both ratios are k-rate, so the stretch may travel over the note.

tube.gloss: whole-number spacings: hollow, with a clear note

bell.gloss: the found body: wide, metallic, no settled note

plate.gloss: far stretched: a plate, all clang and no pitch

drive.note: how bright the air driving the body is, which decides how much of the upper modes ever get woken. measured: centroid 349 -> 526 Hz with the loudness inside 0.2 dB. do NOT reach for the modes' Q instead -- measured over Q 60..1400 that is a 12.3 dB loudness ramp for 56 Hz of colour, i.e. a volume fader wearing a timbre name.

muffled.gloss: worked by dull air; only the lowest mode speaks

room.gloss: the found drive: a machine room

bright.gloss: brighter air, the upper modes come up

hissing.gloss: driven by full-band hiss, all modes lit

techniques.why: divide-down organ / string machine -- a transistor organ, combo organ, theatre organ or Solina-family string synthesizer: ONE master clock divided by twelve integers, exact binary octaves below, and every stop a footage sum off that same RUNNING chain. No key starts a tone -- the chain runs and a key only opens taps onto it. The OCTAVE ranks come off that chain, so unisons and octaves between two keys are EXACT; every other interval is equal-tempered and beats as it does anywhere else. Four mixable stops (`flute` the hollow tibia, `diapason` the bright principal chorus, `reed` the nasal kinura/brass/sax family, `strings` the raw saw bus of a string machine), `age` for how far the chain's integer division strays from equal temperament, and `ensemble` for the three-phase bucket-brigade chorus -- the only thing in the instrument that moves, since the chain itself is rigid.

flute.note: the tibia rank: 8', 4', 2' and 1' voiced close to sines, the lowest rank's own third partial 5 dB above the others', which is what keeps it from going hollow. The woody core of an organ and the closest one gets to a pure tone -- it is what carries a theatre organ's warmth. Raising it does not brighten the sound, it fills it out from below.

closed.gloss: the rank is out; nothing of the tibia is heard

soft.gloss: a thin round underlay beneath the brighter stops

hollow.gloss: the woody tibia clearly present, the sound rounded out

full.gloss: the hollow tibia carries the whole registration

diapason.note: the principal chorus: every octave footage plus the 2 2/3' quint and the 1 3/5' tierce. The bright, singing, church-organ body. The quint and tierce are what give it a metallic edge that no stack of octaves alone can reach.

closed.gloss: the chorus is out; nothing of the principal is heard

blended.gloss: an edge of brightness over the flutes

singing.gloss: the principal chorus carries, bright and vocal

full.gloss: the full chorus, quint and tierce ringing on top

reed.note: the kinura / brass / sax family. The fundamental is gone and a formant rides partials 3 to 7 -- that missing fundamental is exactly what makes a reed nasal, snarling and vocal instead of round. It is the most aggressive of the four stops and by far the peakiest, though the diapason is marginally louder. It holds its shape up to a played 2.5 kHz or so; above that the bandpass's own warping lifts the fundamental back and it turns into a bright square.

nasal.gloss: a pinched, reedy voice cutting through the flues

snarling.gloss: the full kinura -- hard, buzzing and aggressive

strings.note: the raw saw bus of a string machine -- Solina, Logan, Elka -- at 8' and 4'. Alone with `ensemble` up it IS a string machine; under the organ stops it adds a thin bright rasp the flue pipes do not have.

thin.gloss: a faint bright rasp over the organ stops

full.gloss: the bare saw bus of a string machine

age.note: how far the divider chain's tuning strays from equal temperament. The chain divides one master clock by twelve INTEGERS, and that rounding leaves every pitch class its own small fixed offset. This is a DIFFERENT temperament, not a detuning: raising it does not make chords sour, it moves each interval somewhere else. Over the travel the minor third and minor sixth get rougher while the fifth, the sixth and the minor seventh lock TIGHTER than equal temperament manages; octaves and unisons never move at all. 0 is an exactly equal-tempered chain; 1 is the measured Yamaha D-85; above it the chain is coarser than any that was ever built. It is a FIXED offset per key, not a wobble -- a single note cannot show it, two keys together can.

equal.gloss: exactly equal-tempered; the chain's own error taken out

vintage.gloss: the temperament of a real divide-down organ -- at this setting its fourth comes out exactly pure

tempered.gloss: the chain's departure clearly audible in a held chord

coarse.gloss: a coarser chain than was ever built; the temperament plainly its own

ensemble.note: the three-phase bucket-brigade chorus of a string machine: the whole sound through three swept delay lines 120 degrees apart. This is the ONLY thing in the instrument that moves -- the generator chain is rigid by construction. At 0 the tone stands perfectly still: that is the standing-tone escape, not a defect. The knob is a chorus and not a fader; the level holds across its whole travel.

still.gloss: dead still -- the rigid, frozen tone of a bare divider chain

shimmer.gloss: a slow gentle swim over the tone

swimming.gloss: the wide three-phase chorus of a string machine

drowning.gloss: the chorus at full sweep, the pitch visibly swaying

techniques.code:
; LOUDNESS: flute
; LOUDNESS: diapason
; LOUDNESS: reed
; LOUDNESS: strings
; A divide-down organ -- transistor organ, combo organ, string machine. ONE master clock,
; twelve integer divisors, exact binary octaves, and every stop a footage sum off that same
; RUNNING chain: the drawbar principle. Nothing here is keyed to the note -- the chain runs
; and a key only opens taps onto it. The OCTAVE ranks come off that chain, so unisons and
; octaves between two keys are EXACT; every other interval is equal-tempered and beats exactly
; as it does anywhere else. The quint and tierce are taken as exact harmonics of the key rather
; than as their own divider outputs, so they lock where a real chain's would beat slightly.
; Method: top-octave generator, divisors round(478 / 2^(k/12)) -- the MK50240 set. Measured
; against a Yamaha D-85 (49 notes, C3-C7): its tuning error depends on the PITCH CLASS alone
; (0.01 cents spread across octaves) and those divisors reproduce its 12-value pattern to
; 0.03 cents rms. The stop recipes are that organ's own recovered drawbar levels.
; FOLLOWS kfreq: yes.   DECAY: none -- it stands for as long as the key is held.
; It MOVES only through `ensemble`; the chain itself is rigid, and that rigidity is the point.
kflute    = 1.00  ; flute [0..1]: the tibia rank -- 8', 4', 2' and 1' voiced nearly to sines, no quint
kdiapason = 0.45  ; diapason [0..1]: the principal chorus -- octave footages plus the 2 2/3' quint and 1 3/5' tierce
kreed     = 0.00  ; reed [0..1]: the kinura / brass / sax family -- fundamental gone, a formant riding partials 3-7
kstrings  = 0.00  ; strings [0..1]: the raw saw bus of a string machine, 8' and 4'
kage      = 1.00  ; age [0..3]: how far the chain's tuning departs from equal temperament; 1 = the measured D-85
kensemble = 0.45  ; ensemble [0..1]: the three-phase bucket-brigade chorus; 0 is the standing-tone escape

kbase   limit kfreq * koct1, 8.0, 12600.0       ; the host already holds kfreq to 20..12000;
                                                ;   this guards the koct1 product and keeps
                                                ;   log() away from zero
kny     = min(sr * 0.45, 20000)                             ; no voicing corner may pass Nyquist
kpch    = 12 * (log(kbase / 261.6256) / 0.69314718055994531) + 120
                                                ; semitones above C, held positive. NOT logbtwo,
                                                ;   whose table is 0.38 cents out at the bottom of
                                                ;   the keyboard -- harmless now that round() sits
                                                ;   below it, but this line is also the pitch-class
                                                ;   claim's only evidence, and it should be exact.
kkey    = round(kpch)                           ; the KEY picks the divisor, never the bend --
                                                ;   a divider chain has twelve of them, not one
                                                ;   per cent, and rounding the bend would make
                                                ;   the chain a staircase under a glide.
kpc     = kkey - 12 * int(kkey / 12)            ; the pitch class this key asks the chain for
kdiv    = round(478 / pow(2, kpc / 12))         ; the divisor the top-octave chip actually has
kf      = kbase * pow((478 / kdiv) / pow(2, kpc / 12), kage)

at1      vco2 0.5, kf,       10        ; 8'      the rank that sounds the key. The flip-flops
at2      vco2 0.5, kf * 2.0, 10        ; 4'        put out SQUARES, so each rank already
at3      vco2 0.5, kf * 3.0, 10        ; 2 2/3'    carries its own odd partials.
at4      vco2 0.5, kf * 4.0, 10        ; 2'
at5      vco2 0.5, kf * 5.0, 10        ; 1 3/5'
at8      vco2 0.5, kf * 8.0, 10        ; 1'

af1     tone at1, limit(kf * 4.5, 20, kny)         ; the tibia is voiced rank by rank, close to
af2     tone at2, limit(kf * 2.2, 20, kny)         ;   sines -- the lowest rank brightest, its own
af4     tone at4, limit(kf * 4.4, 20, kny)         ;   third partial 5 dB above the others', which
af8     tone at8, limit(kf * 8.8, 20, kny)         ;   is what keeps the stop from going hollow.
aflu    = af1 * 1.00 + af2 * 1.12 + af4 * 0.52 + af8 * 0.50

adia    = at1 * 0.94 + at2 * 0.94 + at3 * 0.31 + at4 * 1.00 + at5 * 0.25 + at8 * 0.38
adia    tone adia, limit(kf * 12.0, 20, kny)      ; the principal is voiced as a chorus, after the sum

apul    vco2 0.5, kf, 2, 0.10         ; the reed's narrow pulse, on the 8' rank
kbpc    limit kf * 4.5, 20, kny * 0.8    ; the reed's formant, kept inside the band
kbpw    limit kf * 5.0, 20, kny * 0.8
ar1     butbp apul, kbpc, kbpw
ared    butbp ar1,  kbpc, kbpw        ; the formant rides the note: partials 3-7, up to
                                      ;   a played ~2.5 kHz. Above that butbp's own warping
                                      ;   lifts the fundamental back and the stop turns from
                                      ;   a reed into a bright square. Declared, not clamped.

as1     vco2 0.5, kf,       0         ; the string machine's saw bus, 8'
as2     vco2 0.5, kf * 2.0, 0         ; and 4'
astr    = as1 * 0.80 + as2 * 0.30

abus    = aflu * kflute * 0.23 + adia * kdiapason * 0.22 + ared * kreed * 1.00 + astr * kstrings * 0.52

ksw1    poscil 1.0, 0.62, giSine               ; the bucket brigade's clock, three phases.
ksw2    poscil 1.0, 0.62, giSine, 0.3333       ;   Its sweep does NOT scale with the knob: a
ksw3    poscil 1.0, 0.62, giSine, 0.6667       ;   brigade always sweeps, and scaling it made
                                               ;   the bottom of the knob a static comb.
ac1     vdelay3 abus, 6.0 + 3.4 * ksw1, 20.0
ac2     vdelay3 abus, 6.0 + 3.4 * ksw2, 20.0
ac3     vdelay3 abus, 6.0 + 3.4 * ksw3, 20.0
amix    = abus + (ac1 + ac2 + ac3) * 0.333 * kensemble
asig    balance amix, abus, 1                  ; the knob is a chorus, not a fader: held against
                                               ;   the dry at a 1 Hz corner, as `analog_osc` holds
                                               ;   its drive. Mixing wet in bare cost 4.4 dB.
